nodes.label: Coordinate Geometry
nodes.note: Two-dimensional analytic geometry unifies straight lines, circles, and conic sections as loci satisfying an equation $$f(x, y) = 0$$. Every JEE problem reduces to forming and manipulating this equation.

nodes.label: Cartesian Foundations
nodes.note: Point geometry on the plane: distance, division, triangle centers, and area are the algebraic toolkit behind every curve. The distance formula is $$d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}$$.

nodes.label: Distance and Section Formulas
nodes.note: The section formula for internal division in ratio $$m:n$$ is $$P = \left( \frac{mx_2 + nx_1}{m + n}, \frac{my_2 + ny_1}{m + n} \right)$$. External division simply flips the signs to $$\frac{mx_2 - nx_1}{m - n}$$.

nodes.label: Internal and External Division
nodes.note: A positive ratio divides internally and a negative ratio divides externally. External division uses $$P = \left( \frac{mx_2 - nx_1}{m - n}, \frac{my_2 - ny_1}{m - n} \right)$$, and the midpoint is the special case $$m = n$$.

nodes.label: Triangle Centers
nodes.note: The centroid is the mean of the vertices, $$G = \left( \frac{x_1 + x_2 + x_3}{3}, \frac{y_1 + y_2 + y_3}{3} \right)$$. The incenter weights vertices by side lengths, $$I = \left( \frac{ax_1 + bx_2 + cx_3}{a + b + c}, \frac{ay_1 + by_2 + cy_3}{a + b + c} \right)$$.

nodes.label: Euler Line
nodes.note: In any non-equilateral triangle the orthocenter $$H$$, centroid $$G$$, and circumcenter $$O$$ are collinear. The centroid divides the segment in the fixed ratio $$\frac{HG}{GO} = \frac{2}{1}$$.

nodes.label: Area and Collinearity
nodes.note: The signed area of a triangle is a third-order determinant, $$\Delta = \frac{1}{2}\begin{vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$$. Setting this determinant to zero is the collinearity test.

nodes.label: Collinearity Condition
nodes.note: Three points are collinear exactly when the area determinant vanishes, equivalently when $$\text{slope}(AB) = \text{slope}(BC)$$. The compact test is $$\begin{vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0$$.

nodes.label: Straight Lines
nodes.note: A line is a first-degree equation $$ax + by + c = 0$$ whose slope is $$m = -a/b$$. All standard forms are reparametrizations of this single equation.

nodes.label: Slope and Inclination
nodes.note: The slope is the tangent of the inclination $$\theta$$ measured from the positive $$x$$-axis, $$m = \tan\theta = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$$. Vertical lines have undefined slope since $$\theta = \pi/2$$.

nodes.label: Standard Line Forms
nodes.note: Point-slope, two-point, slope-intercept, intercept, normal, and parametric forms all describe the same line. The intercept form is $$\frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{b} = 1$$ and the normal form is $$x\cos\alpha + y\sin\alpha = p$$.

nodes.label: Intercept Form
nodes.note: The line cutting intercepts $$a$$ and $$b$$ on the axes is $$\frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{b} = 1$$. The area of the triangle it forms with the axes is $$\frac{1}{2}|ab|$$.

nodes.label: Parametric Distance Form
nodes.note: A point at signed distance $$r$$ along a line of inclination $$\theta$$ through $$(x_1, y_1)$$ is $$\frac{x - x_1}{\cos\theta} = \frac{y - y_1}{\sin\theta} = r$$. Substituting into a curve gives a quadratic in $$r$$ whose roots are the distances to the intersection points.

nodes.label: Angle Between Lines
nodes.note: For slopes $$m_1$$ and $$m_2$$ the acute angle obeys $$\tan\theta = \left| \frac{m_1 - m_2}{1 + m_1 m_2} \right|$$. This ratio is the workhorse for angle-based locus problems.

nodes.label: Parallel and Perpendicular Criteria
nodes.note: Two lines are parallel when their slopes match, which in general form is $$a_1 b_2 - a_2 b_1 = 0$$. They are perpendicular when $$a_1 a_2 + b_1 b_2 = 0$$, i.e. the product of slopes is $$-1$$.

nodes.label: Perpendicular Distance
nodes.note: The distance from $$(x_1, y_1)$$ to the line $$ax + by + c = 0$$ is $$p = \frac{|ax_1 + by_1 + c|}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}}$$. From the origin this reduces to $$p = \frac{|c|}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}}$$.

nodes.label: Distance Between Parallel Lines
nodes.note: For parallel lines with identical $$x$$ and $$y$$ coefficients the separation is $$d = \frac{|c_1 - c_2|}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}}$$. The coefficients of $$x$$ and $$y$$ must first be made equal before applying this formula.

nodes.label: Foot of Perpendicular and Reflection
nodes.note: The foot of the perpendicular from $$(x_1, y_1)$$ to $$ax + by + c = 0$$ satisfies $$\frac{h - x_1}{a} = \frac{k - y_1}{b} = -\frac{ax_1 + by_1 + c}{a^2 + b^2}$$. The mirror image doubles this displacement.

nodes.label: Mirror Image of a Point
nodes.note: The image of $$(x_1, y_1)$$ in the line mirror is given by $$\frac{h' - x_1}{a} = \frac{k' - y_1}{b} = -2\frac{ax_1 + by_1 + c}{a^2 + b^2}$$. The foot is the midpoint of the point and its image.

nodes.label: Family of Lines and Concurrency
nodes.note: The family through the intersection of $$L_1 = 0$$ and $$L_2 = 0$$ is $$L_1 + \lambda L_2 = 0$$ for any real $$\lambda$$. Three lines are concurrent only when a determinant vanishes.

nodes.label: Concurrency Determinant
nodes.note: Three lines $$a_i x + b_i y + c_i = 0$$ are concurrent if and only if $$\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0$$. This is necessary but not sufficient when two lines are parallel.

nodes.label: Angle Bisectors
nodes.note: Points equidistant from two lines give the bisectors $$\frac{a_1 x + b_1 y + c_1}{\sqrt{a_1^2 + b_1^2}} = \pm \frac{a_2 x + b_2 y + c_2}{\sqrt{a_2^2 + b_2^2}}$$. The two bisectors are always mutually perpendicular.

nodes.label: Pair of Straight Lines
nodes.note: A homogeneous second-degree equation $$ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0$$ represents two lines through the origin. The angle between them is $$\tan\theta = \frac{2\sqrt{h^2 - ab}}{|a + b|}$$ and they are perpendicular when $$a + b = 0$$.

nodes.label: Homogenization Technique
nodes.note: To find lines joining the origin to the intersection of a curve and a secant, write the line as $$\frac{lx + my}{-n} = 1$$ and multiply each term to make the curve degree-2. The resulting homogeneous equation represents the two rays $$OA$$ and $$OB$$.

nodes.label: Circles
nodes.note: A circle is the locus of a point at a fixed radius from a center, and its general equation is $$x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$$. The center is $$(-g, -f)$$ and the radius is $$r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}$$.

nodes.label: Standard and General Forms
nodes.note: The central form is $$(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2$$, which expands to the general second-degree form. The radius is real, zero, or imaginary as $$g^2 + f^2 - c$$ is positive, zero, or negative.

nodes.label: Diametric Form
nodes.note: The circle on the segment joining $$A(x_1, y_1)$$ and $$B(x_2, y_2)$$ as diameter is $$(x - x_1)(x - x_2) + (y - y_1)(y - y_2) = 0$$. It is the smallest circle through the two points since the angle in a semicircle is $$90^\circ$$.

nodes.label: Parametric Form
nodes.note: A point on the circle with center $$(h, k)$$ and radius $$r$$ is $$x = h + r\cos\theta, y = k + r\sin\theta$$. The parameter $$\theta$$ is the eccentric angle measured from the horizontal through the center.

nodes.label: Intercepts on Coordinate Axes
nodes.note: The general circle cuts the $$x$$-axis in an intercept of length $$2\sqrt{g^2 - c}$$ and the $$y$$-axis in $$2\sqrt{f^2 - c}$$. It touches an axis when the corresponding expression under the root is zero, i.e. $$g^2 = c$$ or $$f^2 = c$$.

nodes.label: Point Position and Power
nodes.note: For a point $$P(x_1, y_1)$$ the expression $$S_1 = x_1^2 + y_1^2 + 2gx_1 + 2fy_1 + c$$ fixes its position: positive means outside, zero on, negative inside. The power of the point is $$PA \cdot PB = d^2 - r^2 = S_1$$.

nodes.label: Tangents to a Circle
nodes.note: A line $$y = mx + c$$ touches the circle $$x^2 + y^2 = r^2$$ when $$c^2 = r^2(1 + m^2)$$. The tangent at a point $$(x_1, y_1)$$ on the circle is obtained by the $$T = 0$$ substitution.

nodes.label: Slope Form of Tangent
nodes.note: The tangent with slope $$m$$ to $$x^2 + y^2 = r^2$$ is $$y = mx \pm r\sqrt{1 + m^2}$$, touching at $$\left( \mp \frac{mr}{\sqrt{1 + m^2}}, \pm \frac{r}{\sqrt{1 + m^2}} \right)$$. The two signs give the two parallel tangents.

nodes.label: Point Form of Tangent
nodes.note: For the circle $$x^2 + y^2 = r^2$$ the tangent at $$(x_1, y_1)$$ is $$xx_1 + yy_1 = r^2$$. For the general circle the $$T = 0$$ form is $$xx_1 + yy_1 + g(x + x_1) + f(y + y_1) + c = 0$$.

nodes.label: Pair of Tangents and Chord of Contact
nodes.note: From an external point the combined equation of the two tangents is $$SS_1 = T^2$$ and the tangent length is $$L = \sqrt{S_1}$$. The chord joining the contact points is the chord of contact $$T = 0$$.

nodes.label: Director Circle
nodes.note: The locus of the intersection of perpendicular tangents is the director circle $$x^2 + y^2 = 2r^2$$. It is concentric with the original circle and has radius $$\sqrt{2}\,r$$.

nodes.label: Chord of Contact
nodes.note: The chord of contact from an external point $$(x_1, y_1)$$ is $$T = 0$$, namely $$xx_1 + yy_1 + g(x + x_1) + f(y + y_1) + c = 0$$. Its length is $$\frac{2r\sqrt{S_1}}{\sqrt{r^2 + S_1}}$$.

nodes.label: Two Circles Configurations
nodes.note: The number of common tangents depends on $$d$$ versus $$r_1 \pm r_2$$, giving five regimes from four tangents when disjoint down to zero when one circle lies inside the other. The direct and transverse common tangent lengths are $$L_{DCT} = \sqrt{d^2 - (r_1 - r_2)^2}$$ and $$L_{TCT} = \sqrt{d^2 - (r_1 + r_2)^2}$$.

nodes.label: Orthogonality of Circles
nodes.note: Two circles cut orthogonally when the radii at an intersection are perpendicular, so $$d^2 = r_1^2 + r_2^2$$. In general form the algebraic condition is $$2(g_1 g_2 + f_1 f_2) = c_1 + c_2$$, valid only for monic equations.

nodes.label: Radical Axis
nodes.note: The radical axis is the locus of equal power with respect to two circles, found by subtracting the equations to get $$S_1 - S_2 = 0$$. It is always a straight line perpendicular to the line of centers, even when the circles do not intersect.

nodes.label: Family of Circles
nodes.note: Circles through the intersection of two circles form the family $$S_1 + \lambda S_2 = 0$$, and circles through a circle-line intersection form $$S + \lambda L = 0$$. Choosing $$\lambda$$ to cancel a term pins the member through a desired point.

nodes.label: Conic Sections
nodes.note: Every conic is the locus of a point whose distance from a fixed focus bears a constant ratio to its distance from a fixed directrix. The defining relation is $$SP = e \cdot PM$$ where $$e$$ is the eccentricity.

nodes.label: Focus-Directrix Definition
nodes.note: A point $$P$$ lies on a conic when the ratio of its distance from the focus $$S$$ to its perpendicular distance $$PM$$ from the directrix is the constant eccentricity $$e$$, written $$\frac{SP}{PM} = e$$. Squaring $$SP = e \cdot PM$$ yields the second-degree equation of the curve.

nodes.label: Classification by Eccentricity
nodes.note: The value of $$e$$ selects the curve: $$e = 0$$ gives a circle, $$0 < e < 1$$ an ellipse, $$e = 1$$ a parabola, and $$e > 1$$ a hyperbola. This single parameter controls whether the conic is closed, open to one branch, or open to two.

nodes.label: Parabola
nodes.note: The parabola is the conic of eccentricity $$e = 1$$, with standard equation $$y^2 = 4ax$$, focus $$(a, 0)$$, and directrix $$x = -a$$. Its latus rectum has length $$4a$$ and endpoints $$(a, \pm 2a)$$.

nodes.label: Standard Equation
nodes.note: For $$y^2 = 4ax$$ the vertex is the origin, the axis is the $$x$$-axis, and the focus is $$(a, 0)$$. The distance of any point $$(x, y)$$ from the focus equals its distance from the directrix, giving the focal distance $$x + a$$.

nodes.label: Elements and Latus Rectum
nodes.note: The latus rectum is the focal chord perpendicular to the axis, of length $$4a$$ with endpoints $$(a, \pm 2a)$$. The four standard orientations are $$y^2 = \pm 4ax$$ and $$x^2 = \pm 4ay$$, each with the same latus rectum $$4a$$.

nodes.label: Parametric Form
nodes.note: Every point on $$y^2 = 4ax$$ can be written as $$(at^2, 2at)$$ where $$t$$ is the parameter. The parameter is convenient because the slope of the tangent at that point is $$\frac{1}{t}$$ and the tangent is $$ty = x + at^2$$.

nodes.label: Tangents to the Parabola
nodes.note: The tangent at $$(x_1, y_1)$$ is $$yy_1 = 2a(x + x_1)$$, and in slope form the tangent is $$y = mx + \frac{a}{m}$$ touching at $$\left( \frac{a}{m^2}, \frac{2a}{m} \right)$$. From an external point the pair of tangents is $$SS_1 = T^2$$.

nodes.label: Slope Form of Tangent
nodes.note: A line of slope $$m$$ touches $$y^2 = 4ax$$ when it is written as $$y = mx + \frac{a}{m}$$, valid for $$m \neq 0$$. The point of contact is $$\left( \frac{a}{m^2}, \frac{2a}{m} \right)$$, so each slope gives exactly one tangent.

nodes.label: Pair of Tangents
nodes.note: From an external point $$(x_1, y_1)$$ the combined equation of both tangents is $$SS_1 = T^2$$ where $$S \equiv y^2 - 4ax$$ and $$T \equiv yy_1 - 2a(x + x_1)$$. This second-degree equation represents the two straight tangents through the point.

nodes.label: Normals and Focal Chords
nodes.note: The normal at parameter $$t$$ is $$y + tx = 2at + at^3$$, and a chord joining parameters $$t_1$$ and $$t_2$$ has equation $$y(t_1 + t_2) = 2x + 2at_1 t_2$$. A chord through the focus is a focal chord, characterized by $$t_1 t_2 = -1$$.

nodes.label: Focal Chord Property
nodes.note: If the chord joining $$t_1$$ and $$t_2$$ passes through the focus then $$t_1 t_2 = -1$$. Hence when one extremity of a focal chord is $$(at_1^2, 2at_1)$$ the other is $$\left( \frac{a}{t_1^2}, -\frac{2a}{t_1} \right)$$, and the latus rectum is the special case $$t = \pm 1$$.

nodes.label: Chord with Given Midpoint
nodes.note: The chord of $$y^2 = 4ax$$ whose midpoint is $$(x_1, y_1)$$ is given by $$T = S_1$$, that is $$yy_1 - 2a(x + x_1) = y_1^2 - 4ax_1$$. This mirrors the circle result and is derived by equating the midpoint to the average of the intersection roots.

nodes.label: Ellipse
nodes.note: The ellipse is the conic of eccentricity $$0 < e < 1$$ with standard equation $$\frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$$ where $$b^2 = a^2(1 - e^2)$$. The sum of the focal distances of any point is the constant $$SP + S'P = 2a$$.

nodes.label: Standard Equation and Eccentricity
nodes.note: For $$\frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$$ with $$a > b$$ the foci are $$(\pm ae, 0)$$ and the eccentricity is $$e = \sqrt{1 - \frac{b^2}{a^2}}$$. The major axis has length $$2a$$ and the minor axis $$2b$$.

nodes.label: Eccentricity, Foci, and Latus Rectum
nodes.note: The relation $$b^2 = a^2(1 - e^2)$$ ties the axes to the eccentricity, and the latus rectum has length $$\frac{2b^2}{a} = 2a(1 - e^2)$$ with endpoints $$(\pm ae, \pm b^2/a)$$. The directrices are $$x = \pm \frac{a}{e}$$ and the focal radii are $$SP = a - ex$$ and $$S'P = a + ex$$.

nodes.label: Parametric Form
nodes.note: A point on the ellipse is $$(a\cos\theta, b\sin\theta)$$ where $$\theta$$ is the eccentric angle. Substitution verifies the equation instantly since $$\frac{a^2\cos^2\theta}{a^2} + \frac{b^2\sin^2\theta}{b^2} = \cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1$$.

nodes.label: Tangents to the Ellipse
nodes.note: The tangent at $$(x_1, y_1)$$ is $$\frac{xx_1}{a^2} + \frac{yy_1}{b^2} = 1$$, and the slope form is $$y = mx \pm \sqrt{a^2 m^2 + b^2}$$. The tangent at the parametric point is $$\frac{x\cos\theta}{a} + \frac{y\sin\theta}{b} = 1$$.

nodes.label: Slope Form of Tangent
nodes.note: A line $$y = mx + c$$ touches the ellipse when $$c^2 = a^2 m^2 + b^2$$, so the tangents are $$y = mx \pm \sqrt{a^2 m^2 + b^2}$$. The condition $$c^2 = a^2 m^2 + b^2$$ is the tangency test and follows from setting the line-curve discriminant to zero.

nodes.label: Normal to the Ellipse
nodes.note: The normal at the parametric point $$(a\cos\theta, b\sin\theta)$$ is $$ax\sec\theta - by\csc\theta = a^2 - b^2$$. In point form it is $$\frac{a^2 x}{x_1} - \frac{b^2 y}{y_1} = a^2 - b^2$$, obtained from the gradient of the curve.

nodes.label: Auxiliary and Director Circles
nodes.note: The auxiliary circle on the major axis is $$x^2 + y^2 = a^2$$ and supplies the eccentric angle via the perpendicular from a point on the ellipse. The director circle, the locus of perpendicular tangents, is $$x^2 + y^2 = a^2 + b^2$$ and the area enclosed by the ellipse is $$\pi ab$$.

nodes.label: Hyperbola
nodes.note: The hyperbola is the conic of eccentricity $$e > 1$$ with standard equation $$\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$$ where $$b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1)$$. The absolute difference of the focal distances is the constant $$|SP - S'P| = 2a$$.

nodes.label: Standard Equation and Eccentricity
nodes.note: For $$\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$$ the foci are $$(\pm ae, 0)$$ with $$c^2 = a^2 + b^2$$ and the eccentricity is $$e = \sqrt{1 + \frac{b^2}{a^2}}$$. The transverse axis has length $$2a$$ and the conjugate axis $$2b$$.

nodes.label: Eccentricity and Foci
nodes.note: The identity $$c^2 = a^2 + b^2$$ (note the plus sign, opposite to the ellipse) gives $$e = \frac{c}{a} > 1$$ and the foci $$(\pm ae, 0)$$. The directrices are $$x = \pm \frac{a}{e}$$ and the latus rectum is $$\frac{2b^2}{a} = 2a(e^2 - 1)$$.

nodes.label: Asymptotes
nodes.note: The asymptotes are $$y = \pm \frac{b}{a}x$$ and their combined equation is $$\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 0$$, differing from the hyperbola only in the constant term. The angle between them is $$2\tan^{-1}(b/a)$$ and the eccentricity satisfies $$e = \sec\theta$$ when the angle is $$2\theta$$.

nodes.label: Parametric Form
nodes.note: A point on the hyperbola is $$(a\sec\theta, b\tan\theta)$$ since $$\frac{a^2\sec^2\theta}{a^2} - \frac{b^2\tan^2\theta}{b^2} = \sec^2\theta - \tan^2\theta = 1$$. The parameter $$\theta$$ is used exactly as the eccentric angle is used for the ellipse.

nodes.label: Tangents to the Hyperbola
nodes.note: The tangent at $$(x_1, y_1)$$ is $$\frac{xx_1}{a^2} - \frac{yy_1}{b^2} = 1$$ and in slope form $$y = mx \pm \sqrt{a^2 m^2 - b^2}$$, which needs $$a^2 m^2 \ge b^2$$. The parametric tangent is $$\frac{x\sec\theta}{a} - \frac{y\tan\theta}{b} = 1$$.

nodes.label: Slope Form of Tangent
nodes.note: A line $$y = mx + c$$ touches the hyperbola when $$c^2 = a^2 m^2 - b^2$$, giving $$y = mx \pm \sqrt{a^2 m^2 - b^2}$$. Unlike the ellipse, slopes with $$|m| < b/a$$ yield no real tangent because the line would meet both branches.

nodes.label: Normal to the Hyperbola
nodes.note: The normal at $$(x_1, y_1)$$ is $$\frac{a^2 x}{x_1} + \frac{b^2 y}{y_1} = a^2 + b^2$$, again with a plus sign unlike the ellipse. It is derived from the gradient $$\left( \frac{x_1}{a^2}, -\frac{y_1}{b^2} \right)$$ and passes through the point of contact.

nodes.label: Conjugate and Rectangular Hyperbola
nodes.note: The conjugate hyperbola $$\frac{y^2}{b^2} - \frac{x^2}{a^2} = 1$$ shares the same asymptotes, and if $$e_1, e_2$$ are the two eccentricities then $$\frac{1}{e_1^2} + \frac{1}{e_2^2} = 1$$. A rectangular hyperbola has $$a = b$$, perpendicular asymptotes, eccentricity $$e = \sqrt{2}$$, and can be written as $$xy = c^2$$.
